subject: Trading
title: Mental vs. Hard Stops
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mental vs. Hard Stops usable.

hook.text: 'I'll sell if it hits $90' you tell yourself. It hits $90. You hesitate. It hits $85. $80. That mental stop failed.

buildup.text: A mental stop is a price you intend to sell at. A hard stop is an order already placed in the system.

discovery.text: Hard stops execute automatically, removing emotion from the exit. Mental stops need willpower—which fails under stress.

twist.text: Some professionals use mental stops to avoid getting hunted by algorithms that see resting stop orders.

climax.text: For most traders, hard stops are far safer. The discipline required for mental stops is rare and often overestimated.

punchline.text: Place the order. Don't trust your willpower.

quiz.question: Why are hard stops generally safer than mental stops?
options: They execute automatically—removing emotion from the exit
